name: Tswana
notes: Tswana (Setswana) — Sotho-Tswana (Bantu) language, official in Botswana and South Africa, written disjunctively in the Latin script. SKELETON: consonant/vowel-letter table now specified, targeting the South African standard orthography (as the sibling Sotho-Tswana spec `st`/Southern Sotho targets its own SA-standard convention: see AGENTS.md, 'a shared alphabet is not a shared phonology' — the two languages' plain-stop series differ and are NOT copied from one another here). KEY FEATURES (Cole 1955, 'An Introduction to Tswana Grammar'; Wikipedia 'Tswana language' and 'Tswana phonology'): (1) plain ⟨k p t ts tl pj⟩ are EJECTIVE, contrasting with the aspirated ⟨kh ph th tsh tlh⟩ series — the same ejective/aspirate two-way laryngeal contrast Sotho-Tswana languages share, unlike the plain-voiceless system of most other Bantu languages; (2) ⟨b⟩ is an IMPLOSIVE /ɓ/, not a plain voiced stop; (3) ⟨kg⟩ is a velar fricative /x/ (parallel to Southern Sotho's ⟨kg⟩ /x/); (4) ⟨g⟩ (rare, mostly in loans and some dialects) is the voiced velar fricative /ɣ/; (5) the click letter ⟨q⟩/⟨qh⟩ occurs only in a small set of ideophones and Khoisan loanwords, not in the native lexicon; (6) the Botswana orthography differs from the South African one documented here (e.g. Botswana merges some digraphs); mixing the two spelling conventions is OUT OF CONTRACT, matching the same convention-mixing caveat already documented for `st`. Tone is lexically and grammatically contrastive in Tswana but is not marked in the standard orthography and is not asserted here. STRESS EXEMPTION (documented, matching the sibling `st`/Southern Sotho precedent): Tswana word stress is non-contrastive and predictable (fixed, phonetically weak, falling on or near the penultimate mora), not marked in the orthography and not the language's distinctive prosodic feature -- tone carries that role instead (Cole 1955; Wikipedia 'Tswana phonology'). No `stress` block is added; this is a documented exemption, not an omission. RESEARCH: citation-verified 2026-08 (sources wave 4) -- Cole 1955 is a read primary reference grammar (not merely a bibliographic listing); the grapheme table (ejective k/p/t/ts/tl/pj vs aspirate kh/ph/th/tsh/tlh, implosive b, kg=/x/, g=/ɣ/, click q/qh restricted to ideophones/loans) was checked against it and against the cited Wikipedia 'Tswana phonology' article: no discrepancy found. Gold: vox_communis (Common Voice force-aligned, epitran-derived tier, PER 0.40, n=2271; see benchmarks/results.json).
